caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.

The plot illustrates the coverage achieved by four different language models – Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT – as a function of the number of completions (k). The x-axis represents the number of completions, ranging from 2^0 to 2^8, utilizing a logarithmic scale with tick intervals of one unit. The y-axis displays coverage, ranging from approximately 0.22 to 0.92, with tick intervals of 0.02. The blue line represents Llama-3B, beginning at a coverage value of approximately 0.42 at k=20 and increasing to approximately 0.92 at k=256. A dashed cyan line depicts Llama-3B + FT, starting at approximately 0.42 at k=20 and reaching approximately 0.92 at k=256. A light blue line represents Llama-1B, beginning at a coverage value of approximately 0.22 at k=20 and increasing to approximately 0.72 at k=128. Finally, a light green line represents Llama-1B + FT, starting at approximately 0.22 at k=20 and reaching approximately 0.72 at k=128.
